SOURCE: "AutoMix: Automatically Mixing Language Models", Pranjal Aggarwal, Aman Madaan, Ankit Anand, Srividya Pranavi Potharaju, Swaroop Mishra, Pei Zhou, Aditya Gupta, Dheeraj Rajagopal, Karthik Kappaganthu, Yiming Yang, Shyam Upadhyay, Manaal Faruqui, Mausam. Venue: NeurIPS 2024 (footer: "38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2024)"); arXiv:2310.12963v5, 19 Jan 2025. Filename says 2023 (first arXiv version). Code: github.com/automix-llm/automix.

COVERAGE: 88146 of 88146 chars read (main text, references skimmed, all appendices A-E, including prompts). Figures are extracted as axis garbage only, so figure data points were not readable; I did not run the figure-caption script.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: Headline: AutoMix cuts compute cost by over 50% at comparable performance, across five LMs and five datasets.
  number: >50% (abstract); ">2x" (intro)
  setup: Black-box APIs. SLMs are LLaMA2-13B, Mistral-7B and GPT-3.5, with GPT-4 as the LLM. Five context-grounded datasets. N=2 main setting.
  quote: "Experiments across five language models and five challenging datasets show that AutoMix consistently surpasses strong baselines, reducing computational cost by over 50% for comparable performance."
  where: abstract. The intro says "reducing cost by over two times while achieving the same performance".
  Note: the paper counts "five language models" as Mistral-7B, LLaMA2-13B, GPT-3.5, LLaMA2-70B and GPT-4. No table gives the cost-reduction percentage directly. The support is the ΔIBC and cost-performance curves.
- claim: AutoMix with the POMDP router beats FrugalGPT and HybridLLM in ΔIBC on every dataset and SLM. It is the only method with positive gains in all configurations.
  number: Table 1 ΔIBC (%), AutoMix+P vs FrugalGPT vs HybridLLM, columns DIPLOMAT / MUTUAL / COQA / QASPER / QUALITY:
  - Mistral-7B: AutoMix+P 156.8 / 46.7 / 12.4 / 69.3 / 51.6. FrugalGPT 16.8 / 20.3 / -16.7 / 7.7 / 8.1. HybridLLM 67.1 / 3.4 / 10.5 / 0.4 / 2.7.
  - LLaMA2-13B: AutoMix+P 58.5 / 12.4 / 83.1 / 8.5 / 10.3.
  - GPT-3.5: AutoMix+P 151.2 / 18.8 / 65.0 / 114.7 / 24.1.
  - Threshold variant, AutoMix+T: Mistral 149.7 / 46.7 / 12.1 / 67.9 / 33.6. LLaMA 50.1 / 11.8 / 86.5 / -0.2 / 9.4. GPT-3.5 168.2 / 18.3 / 62.7 / 109.8 / 23.5.
  setup: ΔIBC is averaged over five equally sized cost regions. Costs: SLM = 1 unit, LLM = 60 (GPT-3.5), 100 (LLaMA2-13B) or 200 (Mistral-7B) units. 1000 instances sampled per dataset.
  quote: "AutoMix-POMDP is the only method that yields positive gains across all configurations and consistently matches or exceeds the performance of AutoMix-Threshold." Also: "the best performance observed on the DIPLOMAT dataset, averaging 122% across all models."
  where: Section 5.3 and Table 1 (p.8)
  Caveats from the table: Threshold beats POMDP in a few cells (GPT-3.5 DIPLOMAT 168.2 vs 151.2; LLaMA COQA 86.5 vs 83.1). AutoMix+T is negative on LLaMA QASPER (-0.2). FrugalGPT is negative on LLaMA MUTUAL (-8.7), LLaMA DIPLOMAT (-7.0), LLaMA QUALITY (-4.7) and Mistral COQA (-16.7). The text says POMDP "equalling FrugalGPT in the qasper dataset for the LLAMA 2-13 B model" (8.5 vs 9.4, so POMDP is actually slightly lower in the table).
- claim: IBC metric (Incremental Benefit per Cost) measures efficiency of a mixing method relative to always calling the LLM.
  number: formula
  setup: IBC_M = (P_M − P_SLM)/(C_M − C_SLM). IBC_BASE = (P_LLM − P_SLM)/(C_LLM − C_SLM). ΔIBC(M) = (IBC_M − IBC_BASE)/IBC_BASE × 100.
  quote: "A positive IBC lift suggests that M achieves performance increments more cost-effectively than a standalone LLM, whereas a negative lift indicates reduced efficiency"
  where: Section 5.1, Eq. 1, Fig. 3.
  Geometry: IBC is the slope from the SLM point to the method's point. A method above the SLM-LLM line has positive ΔIBC. The baseline is random mixing, i.e. linear interpolation.
- claim: Self-verification is a few-shot, context-grounded entailment check. It is not trained. The same small model generates and verifies.
  number: k>1 samples (8 per question), 3-shot or 4-shot prompt (inconsistent in the text)
  setup: Verifier = the SLM. Samples at high temperature. Verifier probability = fraction of k samples saying "Correct". The same prompt is used for all tasks.
  quote: "we sample k >1 times from the verifier (LMi) with high sampling temperature, and probability is then computed as 1k Pki=1 1{correct = 1}. We use the same 4-shot verification prompt for all tasks and do not train a verifier."
  where: Section 4.1. Appendix B: "For verification, we generate eight samples per question (temperature = 1)". The same appendix later says "temperature=0.7 and draw 8 samples". Listing 4 says "3-shot verifier prompt". Also, 8 verification samples are costed as equal to 1 call: "invoking the verifier 8 times is considered equivalent in cost to calling it once", and Cver = CSLM.
- claim: Self-verification is noisy but informative. Higher verifier probability gives higher precision of correctness on most datasets, with exceptions.
  number: none (figure only)
  quote: "for all datasets, excluding QUALITY and QASPER, a higher verification score generally corresponds to a larger proportion of correct examples" (Fig. 12 caption, LLaMA2-13B as SLM). Also: "For all but QUALITY and QASPER higher verification probability, always higher precision. Even for QASPER, barring 2/9 outliers, the trend generally holds."
  where: Appendix A.1, Fig. 12. "Correct" there means F1 > 0.1. Table 3 shows a verifier miss, where a correct paraphrase is marked Incorrect.
- claim: The POMDP router treats verifier outputs as noisy observations of hidden question difficulty. It can decline to route unsolvable queries to the LLM.
  number: none
  setup: State S = <i, Perf_LM1..Perf_LMN>. Actions: keep the answer or Route_j (j>i). Observations: verifier probabilities (9 discrete values). Reward R = P − λ·C. Transitions are deterministic. Observation model P(o|s) is estimated on the train set via Gaussian KDE. Horizon ≤ N. Solver: AdaOps with particle-filter beliefs, discount γ=1. A simpler tree-search solver is described that reduces the policy to an offline lookup table.
  quote: "in the QASPER dataset using MISTRAL-7B as SLM, POMDP identifies that lower confidence values correspond to such cases, and instead of routing to the LLM as other methods do, returns the SLM answer, saving cost."
  where: Sections 4.2, 5.4, Appendix A.3. The router is a non-LLM component. The authors say it avoids "escalating issues such as hallucination and reasoning errors".
- claim: Low-data regime: the router is trained from as few as 50 examples and beats the supervised baselines there.
  number: 15% ΔIBC at 50 examples; >20% absolute margin over baselines
  setup: Macro-averaged ΔIBC (Fig. 5 left). Baselines FrugalGPT (DistilBERT router) and HybridLLM (DeBERTa router) are trained per domain and assigned zero verifier cost.
  quote: "with just 50 training examples, AutoMix maintains 15% ∆IBC and beats the baselines by more than absolute 20%."
  where: Section 5.4. The appendix says FrugalGPT "narrows the performance gap" as data grows, and that AutoMix has "higher gains visible when dataset size is less than 1000".
- claim: Robust across cost ratios. It gives gains at 1:10, still beats baselines at 20:1, and gains more at 2000:1.
  number: 1:10 / 20:1 / 2000:1
  quote: "even for a cost ratio as low as 1:10, AutoMix begins to deliver good gains for many datasets". Appendix D.2: "Even at a 20:1 ratio (an unlikely, pessimistic scenario for AutoMix), AutoMix outperforms baselines, albeit with smaller margins. Conversely, at a 2000:1 ratio, AutoMix shows even higher improvements."
  where: Section 5.4, Fig. 5 right, App. D.2, Fig. 20. Appendix B inconsistently says "as low as 1:25".
- claim: Out-of-domain generalization: a router trained on one dataset and tested on the other four still beats the baselines.
  number: Table 5 ΔIBC averaged over 5 datasets. AutoMix 28.3 (Mistral-7B) / 31.5 (LLaMA-13B) / 70.9 (GPT-3.5). Frugal 12.5 / 0.0 / 14.3. Hybrid 2.4 / -2.8 / 7.6.
  where: App. D.3
- claim: Overhead is negligible.
  number: POMDP <1ms per query, network latency about 10ms, generation takes seconds
  quote: "At inference time, POMDP takes less than 1ms for every query in the two-model setup."
  where: Section 5.4. Also: "our library can be incorporated in less than five lines of code."
- claim: Three-model results (N=3, SLM, MLM, LLM): AutoMix3 beats FrugalGPT (cascade), Union AutoMix and Chained AutoMix across cost regions. It learns to skip a distractor MLM that underperforms the SLM.
  number: none (curves)
  setup: LLaMA2-13B / Mistral-7B / GPT-3.5 as SLM, LLaMA2-70B as MLM, GPT-4 as LLM. Cascades cannot go SLM to LLM directly. Chained AutoMix "underperforms across the board, as it cannot directly route queries from the SLM to the LLM".
  quote: "AutoMix is able to identify patterns that result in statistically overperforming even the LLM even at roughly half the cost."
  where: Section 5.5, App. C. Fig. 10 is a single case, GPT-3.5 as SLM, LLaMA-70B as MLM, GPT-4 as LLM, DIPLOMAT. The 3-model IBC extension is described in C.1.
- claim: Main-result consistency across the 15 configurations (5 datasets x 3 SLMs).
  quote: "for 13/15 configurations, AutoMix-POMDP is clearly better than all other baselines throughout different operating costs. Even in the remaining 2 cases, AutoMix is competitive and almost equivalent to the baselines."
  where: App. D.1

SETUP DETAILS
- Datasets: QASPER (F1), QUALITY (accuracy, MCQ), COQA (F1), MUTUAL (accuracy), DIPLOMAT (accuracy).
- 1000 instances sampled per dataset's validation split. Context capped at 3500 tokens, retrieved with all-MiniLM-L6-v2.
- Greedy decoding (temp 0) for the SLM and LLM, one sample each. Identical prompts to all models.
- Cost: C = C_SLM + C_ver + w·C_LLM. Pricing is quoted as "$0.225 for LLAMA 2-13 B vs $30 for GPT-4 per 1M tokens".
- Models hosted with vLLM.
- Task accuracy range 30-90%. The SLM-LLM gap ranges from 8% to about 50%.

LIMITS
- Authors concede the method is designed for "dialogue-related or context-grounded reasoning setup", which "does not include tasks like factual question-answering and commonsense reasoning". The context is needed for verification. Applicability "might vary depending on the specific models and datasets used".
- Conclusion says extending to generation tasks, where performance is subjective, is future work.
- When the MLM verifier is uninformative in 3-model setups, gains vanish (Fig. 11, two cases, no significant gain over FrugalGPT).
- Baselines get zero router cost. The AutoMix verifier is costed as one SLM call. The 8-sample verifier cost is treated as free because the context dominates cost.
- Costs are simulated from price ratios, not measured. No real latency or dollar measurements. Cost ratios are an assumption (60/100/200).
- Only black-box API models from 2023-2024 are used. GPT-4 is the only LLM. The authors suggest cheaper strong models might make routing less needed.
- The router needs a labelled train set of <C, q, y_hat, y_LM_i> triplets, which needs inference on all models (a training-time cost).
- ΔIBC can exceed 100% and is a ratio against a baseline slope, so it is not an absolute accuracy or cost saving. No accuracy-at-fixed-cost table is given in text.

BUILDS ON: Chen et al. 2023 (FrugalGPT, baseline); Ding et al. 2024 (HybridLLM, baseline); Åström 1965 (POMDP); Wu et al. 2021 (AdaOps solver); Dagan et al. 2005/2022 and Poliak 2020 (textual entailment framing); Weng et al. 2022/2023 and Jiang et al. 2023b (self-verification); Madaan et al. 2023 (Self-Refine) and Huang et al. 2023b (self-correction is unreliable); Aggarwal et al. 2023 (Adaptive-Consistency); Shaham et al. 2022/2023 (SCROLLS/ZeroSCROLLS prompts); Reimers and Gurevych 2019 (retrieval); Sanh et al. 2019 (DistilBERT) and He et al. 2021 (DeBERTa) for baseline routers; Kwon et al. 2023 (vLLM).

CODE
Verification prompt (Listing 1, p.3): "Context: {context} Question: {question} AI Generated Answer: {generated_answer} Instruction: Your task is to evaluate if the AI Generated Answer is correct, based on the provided context and question. Provide the judgement and reasoning for each case. Choose between Correct or Incorrect. Evaluation:"
Algorithm (Fig. 3 left): answer_query(C,q): As=SOLVE(SLM,C,q); v=SELF-VERIFY(As,C,q); if META-VERIFY(v,As,C,q) return As else return SOLVE(LLM,C,q).
Bellman: V(b) = max_a [R(b,a) + γ Σ_o P(o|b,a) V(b')], with γ=1.
Thresholding router (N=2): "If v ≥ t, it returns LM1's answer, else routes the query to LM2."

FIGURES (captions only; data unreadable in extraction)
- Fig. 1 (p.2): the 3-step pipeline of generate, self-verify, POMDP route. It is the quickest overview.
- Fig. 2 (p.4): worked verifier example (LLaMA2-13B rejects "He took it in 1990").
- Fig. 3 (p.6): algorithm plus the IBC slope picture (green region above the SLM-LLM line, red below).
- Fig. 4 (p.7): the main cost vs performance curves for Mistral-7B/GPT-4 on five datasets. The caption mislabels the SLM legend as LLaMA2-13B.
- Fig. 5 (p.9): left, ΔIBC vs training-set size. Right, normalized ΔIBC vs cost ratio.
- Fig. 6 (p.10): 3-model results.
- Fig. 12 (p.24): verifier probability vs correctness.
- Fig. 18/19: the other two SLMs. Fig. 20: cost-ratio curves.

PROBLEMS
- No embedded instructions found in the PDF.
- Figure axis data came out garbled (some CID-like text on Fig. 5), so no curve values.
- Internal inconsistencies in the paper: verifier shots (3-shot in Listing 4 vs 4-shot in Section 4.1); verifier temperature (1.0 vs 0.7); minimum useful cost ratio (1:10 in Section 5.4 vs 1:25 in App. B); Fig. 4 caption says "LLAMA 2-13 B (SLM)" for a Mistral-7B plot; App. C and Fig. 6 caption say "LLAMA 2-13B, GPT-4 and GPT-4" (typo for LLaMA-70B); App. B cost-ratio text says "GPT-4 and GPT-4"; App. B references "Section 6" for cost ratios, but it is Section 5.4 (App. D.2). The "five language models" count includes LLaMA2-70B, which is used only in the 3-model experiments.
- The 15 statistical-significance claims ("statistically overperforming") give no test details.
